'''Richard John Ackland''' (born 2 August 1958) is a New Zealand former professional [[rugby league]] footballer who played in the 1970s and 1980s, [[Coach (sport)|coach]] in the 1990s, 2000s and 2010s, and scout in the 2000s, and former [[cricket]]er in the 1980s, who works for the [[New Zealand Warriors]] in the [[National Rugby League]]. He represented [[New Zealand national rugby league team|New Zealand]] in 1983.<ref name="Statistics at rugbyleagueproject.org"/><ref name="Coach Statistics at rugbyleagueproject.org"/> His late uncle, [[Ron Ackland|Ron]], also played for New Zealand.<ref name="NZ_Herald_10115130">{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/48-hours-weekend-sport-review/news/article.cfm?c_id=805&objectid=10115130|title=''48 hours:'' Sonny Bill – the future and a reminder of league's follies|author=Chris Rattue|date= 14 March 2005|work=The New Zealand Herald|access-date=10 September 2011}}</ref>

==Background==
Ackland was born in [[Auckland]], New Zealand.

==Playing career==
Ackland played rugby league in New Zealand in the 1980s as a [[Rugby league positions#Forwards|forward]]. In 1981, he won the [[Auckland Rugby League club trophies|Lipscombe Cup]] while playing in the [[Auckland Rugby League]] competition for [[Mt Albert Lions|Mt Albert]]. He also was named man of the match in the 1981 Fox Memorial grand final, after scoring a try.<ref>Coffey, John and Bernie Wood ''Auckland, 100 years of rugby league, 1909–2009'', 2009. {{ISBN|978-1-86969-366-4}}, p. 258.</ref> In 1983, he won the Bert Humphries Memorial for best forward in the competition.

He spent the 1982–83 off-season in [[England]] with the [[Hunslet R.L.F.C.|Hunslet]]. In 1986, he moved to [[New South Wales]], playing for the Murwillumbah Brothers club. In 1987, he joined Wagga Brothers as the captain-coach before returning to Mount Albert in 1989 for one last season.<ref name=704kiwis>Bruce Montgomerie ''Those Who Played'', Montgomerie Publishing, 2004. {{ISBN|0646434071}}</ref>

===Representative career===
In 1983, he made his one and only appearance for the [[New Zealand national rugby league team]], coming off the bench against [[Papua New Guinea national rugby league team|Papua New Guinea]]. Ackland also represented [[Auckland rugby league team|Auckland]] and played in the 1983 draw against [[Hull F.C.]]<ref>Coffey, John and Bernie Wood ''Auckland, 100 years of rugby league, 1909–2009'', 2009. {{ISBN|978-1-86969-366-4}}, p. 260.</ref>

===Cricket career===
Ackland also played [[first-class cricket]] for [[Auckland Aces|Auckland]], as a slow left-arm orthodox bowler. From six appearances he took 10 wickets at 30.50.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/newzealand/content/player/36210.html|title=Richard Ackland|publisher=[[ESPNcricinfo]]}}</ref>

==Coaching career==

===1990s===
Ackland has had a long association with the [[Mt Albert Lions]] and in 1995 coached the [[Auckland Warriors]] under 16s and the Colts side in the [[Lion Red Cup]].<ref>Coffey, John and Bernie Wood ''Auckland, 100 years of rugby league, 1909–2009'', 2009. {{ISBN|978-1-86969-366-4}}, p. 311.</ref> In 1996, he was the club's Development officer and in 1997 he was the under 19 coach.

In 1999, he was made head coach of Mount Albert and coached the Lions to the [[2002 Bartercard Cup]] grand final victory.<ref>Coffey, John and Bernie Wood ''Auckland, 100 years of rugby league, 1909–2009'', 2009. {{ISBN|978-1-86969-366-4}}, p. 333.</ref>

In 2023, he had the honour of being the first head coach of the Mt Albert Mad Dogs Open Age restricted weight team.

===Bulldogs scout===
Ackland worked as a New Zealand-based [[scout (sport)|scout]] for the Australian rugby league club the [[Canterbury Bulldogs]] where he is credited as bringing [[Sonny Bill Williams]], [[Roy Asotasi]] and [[Hutch Maiava]] to the club.<ref name="NZ_Herald_10365830">{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/section/4/story.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=10365830|title=League: Special agent behind enemy lines|author=Michael Brown|date=29 January 2006|work=The New Zealand Herald|access-date=10 September 2011}}</ref>

===Warriors coach===
In 2006, he was appointed the Assistant Coach for the [[New Zealand Warriors]]. In 2010 he was switched with [[Tony Iro]] and Ackland became the Warrior's [[National Youth Competition (rugby league)|Toyota Cup]] coach.<ref name="NZ_Herald_10599491&ref=rss">{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=10599491&ref=rss|title=NRL: Bell wins leading role at Warriors|author=Steve Deane|date=25 September 2009|work=The New Zealand Herald|access-date=10 September 2011}}</ref> The team won the grand final in 2010, the club's first grand final victory, and repeated the feat in 2011. In 2013 he announced he was stepping down from the position at the end of the year.<ref>[http://www.warriors.co.nz/news-display/Ackland%20stepping%20down%20at%20end%20of%202013/76784 Ackland stepping down at end of 2013] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029210719/http://www.warriors.co.nz/news-display/Ackland%20stepping%20down%20at%20end%20of%202013/76784 |date=29 October 2013 }} ''warriors.co.nz'', 11 June 2013</ref>

===Representative coaching===
He was the [[Samoa national rugby league team|Samoan]] head coach and took them to the [[2008 Rugby League World Cup|2008 World Cup]].<ref name="Samoa name World Cup Squad">{{cite web|url=http://www.leagueunlimited.com/article.php?newsid=16750 |title=Samoa name World Cup Squad |publisher=League Unlimited |date=2008-08-05 |access-date=2008-08-06 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717060051/http://www.leagueunlimited.com/article.php?newsid=16750 |archive-date=17 July 2011 }}</ref><ref name="Samoa, Tonga and Fiji name squads">{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/rugby_league/7658506.stm|title=Samoa, Tonga and Fiji name squads|publisher=BBC|date=2008-10-08|access-date=2008-10-09}}</ref>
